title: Raconter au passé et interroger sur les événements
summary: Separate background from events, negate reflexive past forms and form careful inverted questions.
objectives: Distinguish background, bounded events and an earlier past event.
Place negation around a reflexive auxiliary.
Invert compound-past questions with a noun or reflexive pronoun.

sources.label: University of Texas: pronoun placement in compound negation
B1 public topic index (coverage reference only)

sections.title: Choose what the listener sees
paragraphs: The `imparfait` shows a situation from inside: background, a habit or an action in progress. The `passé composé` presents an event as a whole or moves the story forward. Neither tense is chosen simply because an action was long or short: `J'ai travaillé dix ans ici` treats ten years as a completed period.

Form the `imparfait` from present `nous` minus `-ons`, then add `-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient`. `Être` is exceptional: `j'étais, tu étais, il/elle/on était, nous étions, vous étiez, ils/elles étaient`. A `plus-que-parfait` puts an event before a past reference point: use the `imparfait` of `avoir` (`avais, avais, avait, avions, aviez, avaient`) or `être` (`étais, étais, était, étions, étiez, étaient`) plus the participle, keeping the compound-past auxiliary and agreement rules.
points: `Parler` in the `imparfait`: `je parlais, tu parlais, il/elle/on parlait, nous parlions, vous parliez, ils/elles parlaient`.
Vocabulary: `une alarme` (feminine), an alarm; `un entretien` (masculine), an interview or maintenance session.

examples.english: It was raining when the alarm rang.
examples.note: The rain is background; the alarm advances the story.

examples.french: Pendant trois ans, elle **a travaillé** dans ce laboratoire.
examples.english: For three years, she worked in this laboratory.
examples.note: A long period can still be viewed as a completed whole.

examples.french: Nous **avions fermé** les fenêtres avant l'orage.
examples.english: We had closed the windows before the storm.
examples.note: The closing precedes the past storm.

examples.french: Chaque matin, je **prenais** le même bus.
examples.english: Every morning, I used to take the same bus.
examples.note: A repeated past habit seen without a specific completed boundary.

sections.title: Keep the pronoun with the auxiliary
paragraphs: A reflexive verb includes `me`, `te`, `se`, `nous`, `vous` or `se` before its auxiliary `être`. In a written negative compound past, the order is subject + `ne` + reflexive pronoun + `être + pas` + participle. `Ne` and the reflexive pronoun elide before vowels where needed.

For `se lever`: `je ne me suis pas levé/levée`; `tu ne t'es pas levé/levée`; `il ne s'est pas levé`; `elle ne s'est pas levée`; `on ne s'est pas levé`; `nous ne nous sommes pas levés/levées`; `vous ne vous êtes pas levé/levée/levés/levées`; `ils ne se sont pas levés`; `elles ne se sont pas levées`. The listed endings depend on the people concerned. Not every reflexive participle agrees automatically: `elle s'est lavé les mains` has a following direct object; `elles se sont parlé` has an indirect reflexive object.
points: `Jamais` and `plus` can occupy `pas`'s position: `elle ne s'est jamais trompée`; `elle ne s'est plus déplacée`.

examples.french: Lina **ne s'est pas réveillée** à temps.
examples.english: Lina did not wake up in time.
examples.note: `Pas` follows `est`, not the infinitive or the participle.

examples.french: Nous **ne nous sommes pas trompés** d'adresse.
examples.english: We did not get the address wrong.
examples.note: A mixed or all-male group uses `trompés` here.

mistakes.why: `Pas` comes immediately after the auxiliary in this construction.

sections.title: Move the auxiliary, not the participle
paragraphs: In a careful or formal question, invert the auxiliary with the subject pronoun: `a-t-elle compris?` The participle stays after that unit. With a noun subject, keep the noun first and repeat it with the matching pronoun: `Les candidates ont-elles compris?` Insert `-t-` between a vowel-ending auxiliary and `il/elle/on` when needed: `a-t-il`. Do not add another `t` to `est-il` or `ont-ils`.

For reflexive questions, the reflexive pronoun stays before the auxiliary: `s'est-elle levée?` With a noun, combine the two patterns: `Lina s'est-elle levée?` A negative question frames the same auxiliary unit: `Lina ne s'est-elle pas levée?` In ordinary conversation, `est-ce que` or a rising voice is often more natural; inversion is not obligatory in every question.
points: Use hyphens in the inverted auxiliary-pronoun unit and around inserted `-t-`.
Question punctuation does not replace the required subject pronoun in noun inversion.

examples.english: Did the caretaker hear the alarm?
examples.note: The noun is retained; `il` repeats it after `a`.

examples.french: Les visiteuses **se sont-elles présentées** à l'accueil?
examples.english: Did the visitors introduce themselves at reception?

examples.note: Addressing one man; for one woman, `souvenue`.
`Ne` precedes `s'`; `pas` follows the inverted auxiliary unit.

mistakes.why: Invert the auxiliary `ont`, not the participle `compris`.

sections.title: Un groupe avec moi ou toi dans une question
paragraphs: A noun group containing `moi` is repeated by `nous` in an inverted question; a group containing `toi` but not `moi` is repeated by `vous`. This changes the auxiliary as well as the pronoun: `le responsable et moi avons-nous...`, `la responsable et toi avez-vous...`. Do not automatically use `ils` or `elles` just because two people are named.

For a reflexive verb, one `nous/vous` before the auxiliary belongs to the verb and a second after it repeats the subject. In `le responsable et moi nous sommes-nous inscrits?`, the first `nous` is reflexive and the second `nous` is the inverted subject pronoun. Neither is an accidental duplicate. Match participle agreement to the actual group where that verb requires it.
points: These written question patterns are formal. `Est-ce que` with ordinary subject order is often easier in conversation.

examples.french: La responsable et moi **avons-nous choisi** la bonne date ?
examples.english: Have the manager and I chosen the right date?
examples.note: A group containing the speaker is `nous`; the following object leaves `choisi` unchanged.

examples.french: Le formateur et toi **avez-vous confirmé** l'horaire ?
examples.english: Have the trainer and you confirmed the schedule?
examples.note: A group containing the addressee but not the speaker is `vous`.

examples.french: La responsable et moi **nous sommes-nous inscrites** au même atelier ?
examples.english: Have the manager and I registered for the same workshop?
examples.note: Both people are women here. The first `nous` is reflexive, the second is the subject pronoun; `inscrites` agrees with the group.

practice.prompt: Choose the background in a story: Il ___ froid quand nous sommes sortis.
practice.explanation: The instruction treats the cold as surrounding background.

practice.prompt: Insert only the missing words: Lina ne ___ pas levée. Use se lever in the passé composé.
practice.explanation: The reflexive pronoun precedes the auxiliary être.

practice.prompt: Supply only the inverted auxiliary-pronoun unit: Le train ___ quitté la gare? Use avoir and il.
Supply only the missing unit: Les enfants ___ couchés? Use se coucher in the passé composé with inversion.
practice.explanation: Se stays before the auxiliary; ils follows sont.

practice.prompt: Rewrite exactly in the negative with ne ... pas: Elle s'est arrêtée.
practice.explanation: Ne precedes s'est; pas follows est.

practice.prompt: Turn into a noun-subject inverted question: Les techniciens ont vérifié le câble.
answers: Les techniciens ont-ils vérifié le câble?
practice.explanation: Keep the noun and repeat it as ils after ont.

practice.prompt: Turn into an inverted question: Elle s'est reposée.
practice.explanation: The reflexive s' stays attached to est, not to the participle.

practice.prompt: Supply the inverted unit: La directrice ___ reçu votre message? Use avoir and elle.
practice.explanation: A vowel-ending a needs -t- before elle.

practice.prompt: Supply attendre in the imparfait: Nous ___ quand le téléphone a sonné.
practice.explanation: Attendre uses attend- plus -ions for ongoing background.

practice.prompt: Supply fermer in the plus-que-parfait: À mon arrivée, ils ___ le magasin.
practice.explanation: The closing had already occurred before the past arrival.

practice.prompt: Choose the form presenting a ten-year job as a completed period.
choices: Elle a travaillé ici pendant dix ans.
Elle travaillait ici quand je l'ai rencontrée.
answers: Elle a travaillé ici pendant dix ans.
practice.explanation: The passé composé can package a long period as a whole.

practice.prompt: Supply the missing negative group: Nous ___ trompées. Use ne ... pas and se tromper in the passé composé.
practice.explanation: Ne + nous + sommes + pas precedes the participle.

practice.prompt: Turn into an inverted question retaining the noun: Amina s'est inscrite.
practice.explanation: Retain Amina and place elle after est.

practice.prompt: Rewrite with ne ... jamais: Il s'est plaint.
practice.explanation: Jamais takes the same position after the auxiliary as pas.

practice.prompt: Supply être in the imparfait: Vous ___ déjà sur place.
practice.explanation: Être has the exceptional imparfait stem ét-.

practice.prompt: Supply only the inverted unit: ___ rappelé l'heure du rendez-vous? Use vous and se rappeler in the passé composé.
practice.explanation: Reflexive vous precedes êtes; subject vous follows it. Rappelé stays unchanged before its following direct object.

practice.prompt: Supply avoir and its inverted subject pronoun: Le jury et moi ___ retenu la même candidature ?
practice.explanation: A group containing moi is repeated by nous; the auxiliary must be avons.

practice.prompt: Supply avoir and its inverted subject pronoun: Ta sœur et toi ___ reçu les invitations ?
practice.explanation: A group containing toi but not the speaker is vous, paired with avez.

practice.prompt: Complete the reflexive and inverted auxiliary-pronoun group only: Les autres bénévoles et moi ___ retrouvés devant la mairie ? Use se retrouver in the passé composé.
practice.explanation: Reflexive nous stays before sommes; the subject pronoun nous follows it with a hyphen. Both are required.

production_task.prompt: A colleague missed a meeting. Write a brief account with background, one completed event and one earlier event. Add a negative reflexive sentence and a noun-subject inverted question you could use in a formal follow-up.
production_task.model_answer: Il pleuvait et le bus avançait lentement. Lina avait oublié son téléphone. Elle est arrivée après la réunion, mais elle ne s'est pas découragée. La responsable a-t-elle reçu son courriel?
production_task.translation: It was raining and the bus was moving slowly. Lina had forgotten her phone. She arrived after the meeting, but she did not lose heart. Did the manager receive her email?
rubric: Make the three time viewpoints distinguishable.
Keep the reflexive pronoun before `être` and `pas` after it.
Invert the auxiliary and repeat the noun with a matching subject pronoun.
Use subject agreement only where the construction requires it.
